summary_zh: 用被動語態說明飯店的流程與事後報告（Breakfast is served…／I was told…／Your room has been upgraded），並在房間沒準備好時禮貌地問清楚、爭取補償。

vocab.definition: having accepted more bookings than there are rooms or seats
vocab.example: The hotel was overbooked, so two guests had to stay somewhere else.
vocab.example_zh: 飯店超額訂房，所以有兩位客人得住到別的地方。

vocab.definition: given to customers free of charge
vocab.example: Bottled water and coffee are complimentary in every room.
vocab.example_zh: 每間客房的瓶裝水和咖啡都是免費招待的。

vocab.definition: useful or pleasant facilities at a place, such as a gym, a pool or free Wi-Fi
vocab.example: The amenities include a rooftop pool and a 24-hour gym.
vocab.example_zh: 飯店設施包括頂樓泳池和 24 小時健身房。

vocab.zh: 住宿期間的額外消費（如迷你吧、客房服務）
vocab.definition: extra costs during a hotel stay, such as the minibar or room service, on top of the room price
vocab.example: A small hold is placed on your card to cover any incidental charges.
vocab.example_zh: 飯店會在你的卡上預先保留一小筆金額，用來支付可能的額外消費。

vocab.definition: permission to leave your hotel room later than the usual time
vocab.example: Could I get a late checkout? My flight isn't until 6 p.m.
vocab.example_zh: 可以延後退房嗎？我的班機晚上六點才飛。

vocab.zh: 升等（換到更好的房間或座位）
vocab.definition: a move to a better room, seat or service, often at no extra cost
vocab.example: Because of the mix-up, they gave me a free upgrade to a suite.
vocab.example_zh: 因為搞錯了，他們免費幫我升等到套房。

vocab.definition: to do something good that reduces the harm of an earlier problem
vocab.example: The hotel offered us free breakfast to make up for the long wait.
vocab.example_zh: 飯店提供免費早餐，彌補我們等了那麼久。

vocab.definition: to deal with a problem or arrangement until it is fixed
vocab.example: Give me five minutes and I'll sort out the problem with your booking.
vocab.example_zh: 給我五分鐘，我會把你訂房的問題處理好。

reading.title: Arriving to Find There's No Room
paragraphs: Last month, Kevin Lin arrived at a Taipei hotel at 11 p.m. after a long day of meetings. He was run-down and felt like he was coming down with a cold. At the front desk, he was told that the hotel was overbooked and his room was no longer available.

This happens more often than most guests think. Hotels expect a few people to cancel, so extra bookings are accepted on busy nights. When everyone shows up, some guests have to be moved. At most chain hotels, the process is clearly set out: the guest is offered a room at a nearby hotel, the first night is paid for by the original hotel, and transport is usually arranged as well.

Kevin's case was handled by a new receptionist who was still learning the ropes. She admitted that the booking system had a steep learning curve. Still, she called her manager, and they managed to sort out the problem within twenty minutes. A room was found after all, and Kevin was given an upgrade to a suite, a complimentary breakfast and a late checkout to make up for the trouble.

Travel experts say guests should stay calm but ask clear questions. Is the new room paid for? Will my loyalty points carry over? Are the same amenities included? It also helps to check your card: at check-in, a hold for incidental charges is usually placed on it, and it can take several days to be released.

As for Kevin, he bought some over-the-counter cold medicine in the lobby shop and went straight to bed. "I could see at a glance that the front desk was overwhelmed, and at first it looked like a disaster," he said. "In the end, it was the best night of the trip."

questions.q: According to the article, why do hotels accept more bookings than they have rooms?
options: Their booking systems often make mistakes.
They expect some guests to cancel.
Some rooms are always closed for cleaning.
Business travelers usually book at the last minute.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：Hotels expect a few people to cancel, so extra bookings are accepted on busy nights. 飯店預期會有人取消，所以忙的晚上會多收訂房。

questions.q: What did Kevin receive in the end?
options: A room at a nearby hotel and a free taxi
A refund for his first night
An upgrade, a free breakfast and a late checkout
Free cold medicine from the lobby shop
questions.explain_zh: 第三段最後：Kevin was given an upgrade to a suite, a complimentary breakfast and a late checkout。感冒藥是他自己去買的（he bought…）。

questions.q: What can we infer about the receptionist?
options: She had given Kevin's room to a friend.
She was the hotel's manager that night.
She refused to help until Kevin complained.
She was not yet confident using the booking system.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第三段說她 still learning the ropes（還在學怎麼做），也承認系統 had a steep learning curve（不好上手），而且要打電話問經理，可見她對訂房系統還不熟。

grammar.point: Passive voice in reports and processes
grammar.point_zh: 被動語態：說明流程與寫報告

guide.key_zh: 重點在「事情被怎麼處理」、不必說誰做的：be + p.p.；時態由 be 動詞決定。

uses.label_zh: 固定流程、規定（一直都這樣）
uses.note_zh: 說明書、飯店規定最常用

uses.label_zh: 報告裡說過去發生的事
uses.note_zh: I was told…／Two guests were moved…

uses.label_zh: 到現在已經處理好的結果

mistakes.why_zh: be 動詞後面要接過去分詞（served），不能接原形

mistakes.wrong: Your room has been upgrade to a suite.
mistakes.right: Your room has been upgraded to a suite.
mistakes.why_zh: has been 後面一樣要接過去分詞（upgraded），別漏掉 -ed

mistakes.wrong: A mistake was happened with my booking.
mistakes.right: A mistake happened with my booking.
mistakes.why_zh: happen 不能接受詞，所以沒有被動語態

examples.en: Breakfast is served in the lobby from 6:30 to 10 a.m.
examples.zh: 早餐在大廳供應，時間是早上六點半到十點。

examples.en: Two guests were moved to a nearby hotel last night.
examples.zh: 昨晚有兩位客人被安排到附近的飯店。

examples.en: Your room has already been cleaned.
examples.zh: 您的房間已經打掃好了。

exercises.q: At this hotel, rooms ___ (clean) every day between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m.
exercises.explain_zh: every day 是固定流程，房間是「被打掃」→ 現在式被動 are + p.p.：are cleaned。

exercises.q: Last night, two guests ___ (move) to another hotel because we were overbooked.
exercises.explain_zh: Last night 是過去時間，客人是「被安排」換飯店 → was/were + p.p.；主詞 two guests 是複數，用 were moved。

exercises.q: Good news! Your room ___ (just / upgrade) to a suite.
exercises.explain_zh: just 表示剛處理好、結果到現在 → has/have + been + p.p.；主詞 your room 是單數，用 has just been upgraded（just 放在 has 後面）。美式英文也常說 was just upgraded。

exercises.q: At most hotels, a hold for incidental charges ___ (place) on your card at check-in.
exercises.explain_zh: At most hotels … at check-in 是每次入住都一樣的固定流程，主詞 a hold 單數、是「被放上」→ is placed。

exercises.q: From our incident report: "On Monday, the guest's booking ___ by mistake."
options: canceled
was canceled
has canceled
was cancel
exercises.explain_zh: 訂房是「被取消」，On Monday 是過去時間 → was + p.p.：was canceled。canceled、has canceled 是主動；was cancel 少了 -ed。

exercises.q: So far this month, 35 complaints ___ about the Wi-Fi.
options: have received
were receiving
have been received
are receive
exercises.explain_zh: So far this month 是「到現在為止」的結果，投訴是「被收到」→ have been + p.p.：have been received。have received 是主動，意思變成「投訴收到了東西」。

review.point: Indirect questions: Could you tell me where…
review.point_zh: 間接問句：Could you tell me where…

exercises.q: (Where is the shuttle bus?) Could you tell me ___?
exercises.explain_zh: 間接問句要改回直述句的順序：主詞在前、動詞在後 → where the shuttle bus is，不是 where is the shuttle bus。

exercises.q: (What time does breakfast start?) Do you know ___?
exercises.explain_zh: 拿掉助動詞 does，動詞改回 starts（主詞 breakfast 是單數）→ what time breakfast starts。

exercises.q: (Is the gym open 24 hours?) Could you tell me ___?
exercises.answer: if the gym is open 24 hours
accept: whether the gym is open 24 hours
if the gym is open twenty-four hours
whether the gym is open twenty-four hours
exercises.explain_zh: Yes/No 問題變成間接問句要加 if 或 whether，再用直述句順序 → if the gym is open 24 hours。

guide.key_zh: Could you tell me／Do you know 後面改用「主詞＋動詞」順序，不加 do／does／did。

uses.label_zh: 問 wh- 問題（哪裡、什麼時候、多久…）
uses.form: Could you tell me + where / when / how long + S + V
uses.signal: Could you tell me / Do you know
uses.note_zh: where is it → where it is

uses.label_zh: 問「是不是／有沒有」（yes/no 問題）
uses.form: Do you know + if / whether + S + V
uses.note_zh: 原本沒有疑問詞，就補 if 或 whether

uses.label_zh: 用直述句帶出問題，更委婉
uses.form: I was wondering + if / wh- + S + V
uses.signal: I was wondering / I'd like to know

mistakes.wrong: Could you tell me where is the returns desk?
mistakes.right: Could you tell me where the returns desk is?
mistakes.why_zh: 間接問句裡要用直述句順序：主詞 the returns desk 放在 is 前面

mistakes.wrong: Do you know when does the store close?
mistakes.right: Do you know when the store closes?
mistakes.why_zh: 不加 does，動詞直接變化：the store closes

mistakes.wrong: Can you tell me do you have this in black?
mistakes.right: Can you tell me if you have this in black?
mistakes.why_zh: yes/no 問題要用 if 或 whether 接起來

listening.title: My Room Isn't Ready

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Hi, I have a reservation under Daniel Wu. Two nights, a king room.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Welcome, Mr. Wu. Let me check. I'm afraid your room isn't ready yet. It's still being cleaned.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Oh no. Could you tell me how long it'll take? My allergies have flared up, and I really need to lie down.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: I'm so sorry. Rooms are usually cleaned by three o'clock. Our new housekeeper has been learning the routine for two weeks. That's why we're a bit behind today. It should be ready in about forty minutes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Forty minutes is fine, I guess. Do you know if there's somewhere quiet I can wait?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Of course. You're welcome to wait in our lounge, and the drinks there are complimentary. Only two guests have used it since lunch, so it's nice and quiet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Thanks. Also, I'm a member of your rewards program. Will the points from this stay carry over to next year?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Yes, they will. Points don't expire for two years, and the ones from this stay will be added to your account within 48 hours of checkout.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Great. And since I've been kept waiting, is a late checkout possible on Sunday?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Let me sort that out for you. All set. A 2 p.m. checkout has been added to your booking. I'll call you as soon as your room is ready.

questions.q: Why can't Daniel go to his room right away?
options: It is still being cleaned.
It has been given to another guest.
His booking was made for the wrong night.
The hotel is overbooked.
questions.explain_zh: Grace 說：your room isn't ready yet. It's still being cleaned.（房間還在打掃中）

questions.q: What does Grace offer Daniel while he waits?
options: A free upgrade to a suite
Free drinks in the lounge
Medicine for his allergies
Extra points for his account
questions.explain_zh: Grace 說可以去 lounge 等，而且 the drinks there are complimentary（飲料免費）。

questions.q: Why does Daniel most likely ask for a late checkout?
options: His flight on Sunday leaves in the evening.
He wants to use the gym before he leaves.
He feels the hotel should make up for the delay.
Late checkout is included in his rewards program.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：他說 since I've been kept waiting（既然讓我等了這麼久），才提出延後退房，意思是希望飯店補償這次的延誤。對話沒有提到班機或健身房。

dictation: Rooms are usually cleaned by three o'clock.
Only two guests have used it since lunch, so it's nice and quiet.
Our new housekeeper has been learning the routine for two weeks.

shadowing: Could you tell me how long it'll take?
I'm afraid your room is still being cleaned.
A late checkout has been added to your booking.
Do you know if breakfast is included?

prompts.question: You arrive at a hotel and your room isn't ready. Ask the receptionist two polite questions, starting with "Could you tell me…" and "Do you know if…".
prompts.question_zh: 你到了飯店，房間還沒準備好。用 Could you tell me… 和 Do you know if… 開頭，禮貌地問櫃檯兩個問題。用安靜模式打字也算。
hints: Do you know if I can…
prompts.sample: Could you tell me when my room will be ready? Do you know if I can leave my bags here?

prompts.question: A new guest asks how things work at the hotel. Explain two hotel rules in one or two sentences, using the passive (for example "is served", "are cleaned").
prompts.question_zh: 一位剛入住的客人問飯店的規定。用被動語態（例如 is served、are cleaned）說一兩句，說明兩條規定。用安靜模式打字也算。
prompts.sample: Breakfast is served in the lobby from 6:30 to 10. Rooms are cleaned every day unless you hang the Do Not Disturb sign on your door.

writing.task: Your hotel check-in went badly last weekend. Write a short email to the hotel manager in three short parts: (1) what happened when you arrived (use the passive, e.g. "I was told…"), (2) how the problem was handled, and (3) what you would like the hotel to do now. Don't join two complete sentences with only a comma.
writing.task_zh: 上週末你入住飯店時很不順。寫一封短信給飯店經理，分三小段：(1) 抵達時發生了什麼事（用被動語態，例如 I was told…）；(2) 問題後來怎麼被處理；(3) 你希望飯店現在怎麼做。不要只用逗號把兩個完整的句子接在一起。
writing.sample:
Dear Ms. Chen,

I stayed at your hotel last weekend. When I arrived on Friday night, I was told that my room was not ready. I was asked to wait in the lobby for almost an hour.

The receptionist was friendly, but she seemed new. She was still learning the ropes, and nobody was sent to help her. In the end, I was given a room at 11:30 p.m.

I understand that mistakes happen. However, I would like to know how you plan to make up for the delay. Could you please sort out a partial refund for the first night?

Best regards,
Daniel Wu
checklist_zh: 三小段都有寫到：發生什麼事、怎麼處理、希望怎麼補償
被動語態有寫成 be + p.p.（was told、was given），沒有漏掉 be 或 -ed
三個指定用語都有用上
沒有只用逗號把兩個完整句子接在一起

translation.zh: 每天早上六點半到十點，早餐在二樓的餐廳供應。
translation.en: Breakfast is served in the second-floor restaurant from 6:30 to 10 a.m. every day.

Breakfast is served every day from 6:30 to 10 a.m. in the restaurant on the second floor.
Breakfast is served in the restaurant on the second floor from 6:30 to 10 every day.

translation.zh: 您的訂房已經改成兩間相連的房間了。
translation.en: Your booking has been changed to two connecting rooms.
alt: Your reservation has been changed to two connecting rooms.
Your booking has already been changed to two connecting rooms.

translation.zh: 自從我們換了訂房系統之後，客訴已經減少了 30%。
translation.en: Complaints have dropped by 30% since we changed the booking system.
alt: Complaints have gone down by 30% since we changed the booking system.
Complaints have fallen by 30% since we changed the booking system.
Complaints have decreased by 30% since we changed the booking system.
Since we changed the booking system, complaints have dropped by 30%.

translation.zh: 那位新來的櫃檯人員從早上就一直在處理客人的問題。
translation.en: The new receptionist has been dealing with guests' problems since this morning.
alt: The new receptionist has been handling guests' problems since this morning.
The new receptionist has been dealing with guests' issues since this morning.
The new front desk clerk has been dealing with guests' problems since this morning.
The new receptionist has been dealing with guest problems since this morning.

translation.zh: 她已經幫十二位客人辦好入住了。
translation.en: She has already checked in twelve guests.
alt: She has checked in twelve guests.
She has already checked twelve guests in.
She has checked in twelve guests already.
She has already checked in 12 guests.

replies.zh: 今天翻譯第 4、5 題是一組對照：has been dealing with（從早上一直在做、還沒做完）vs has already checked in twelve guests（已經完成、有數量的結果），請你自己寫寫看兩種形式；聽寫第 3 句也有 has been learning。

reading.title: Who Gets Walked?
paragraphs: In the hotel business, there's a polite name for one of the industry's least popular practices. When a hotel is overbooked and a guest with a confirmed reservation is sent to another property, that guest has been "walked." Front desk staff dread it, guests resent it, and yet on busy nights it is almost unavoidable.

The logic is simple enough. On any given night, a certain share of reservations turn out to be no-shows or last-minute cancellations. Revenue managers study years of data and deliberately sell more rooms than the hotel actually has, betting that the numbers will even out. Most of the time, the bet pays off. When it doesn't, someone at the desk has to break the news.

Who gets walked is rarely random. Guests on a single-night stay are usually chosen first, since moving them disrupts the fewest plans. Loyalty members, guests with disabilities and families with small children tend to be protected. Late arrivals are also at risk: by 10 p.m., the decision has often been made already, and the last few rooms have been held for guests who are considered harder to move.

What happens next is largely scripted. The walked guest is booked into a comparable hotel nearby, the room is paid for, and a taxi is called. Many chains go further, comping a future night or adding bonus points to soften the blow. Experienced managers say the tone matters as much as the compensation. "You can't undo the inconvenience," one told an industry magazine, "but you can make sure nobody leaves the lobby feeling like a number."

For travelers, the lesson is to call ahead if they'll be arriving late, and to stay polite. Staff have more discretion than most people realize, and a calm guest is far more likely to end up with a generous fix.

questions.q: What does it mean when a guest is "walked"?
options: They are asked to wait in the lobby until a room is cleaned.
They are sent to another hotel because their hotel is overbooked.
They are given a free night because of a complaint.
They are moved to a smaller room in the same hotel.
questions.explain_zh: 第一段：When a hotel is overbooked and a guest… is sent to another property, that guest has been "walked."（超訂時被送到另一家飯店）

questions.q: Why does the writer advise travelers to call ahead if they'll arrive late?
options: Late arrivals have to pay a higher room rate.
The front desk closes at 10 p.m. at most hotels.
Late guests are more likely to be walked if the hotel doesn't know they're coming.
Taxis are hard to find late at night.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第三段說 Late arrivals are also at risk，到晚上十點常常已經決定好要把誰送走、剩下的房間留給「比較難搬走」的客人。所以先打電話告知，比較不容易被送走。

questions.q: What does the manager's quote suggest?
options: How staff treat walked guests matters as much as what they give them.
Hotels should stop overbooking completely.
Guests who complain loudly get better compensation.
Most walked guests never return to the hotel.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：前一句 the tone matters as much as the compensation，經理說 make sure nobody leaves the lobby feeling like a number（別讓客人覺得自己只是個數字），重點是對待客人的態度。

listening.title: Being Walked at Midnight

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Mr. Hale? Hi, I'm Priya, the night manager. I'm afraid I've got some bad news about tonight—

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Let me guess. You've given my room away.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Well, not exactly. We're overbooked, and, um, a few guests are being moved to the Riverside Hotel down the street.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Seriously? I booked this three months ago. And I've got a presentation at eight tomorrow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: I completely understand. Your room there has already been paid for, and a taxi's been called. It'll be here in five minutes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Okay, but is the Riverside anywhere near the convention center? Because if I get stuck in traffic—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: It's actually closer. About a ten-minute walk, tops.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Huh. Well, that's something, I guess. What about my points?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: They'll be added as if you'd stayed here. And we'd like to comp your next night with us, just to make up for the hassle.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Marcus
lines.text: Fine. I'm too tired to argue anyway. Could you at least put all that in writing?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Already done. It's all been emailed to you. The Riverside will also send a confirmation within the hour.

questions.q: Why is Marcus upset at first?
options: He booked months ago and has an early presentation.
The taxi is going to be very late.
He has lost his loyalty points.
The Riverside Hotel is far from the convention center.
questions.explain_zh: Marcus 說：I booked this three months ago. And I've got a presentation at eight tomorrow.（三個月前就訂了，明早八點還要簡報）

questions.q: Why does Marcus seem to calm down?
options: Priya gives him a room in the same hotel after all.
The new hotel is closer to where he needs to be, and he is offered something extra.
He gets a full refund for his stay.
Priya agrees to drive him to the convention center.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：聽到新飯店離會議中心更近（It's actually closer）後，他說 that's something；之後又得到點數照算和免費住一晚，就不再爭了。

questions.q: What does Priya offer to make up for the problem?
options: A suite upgrade at the Riverside
Breakfast at the convention center
A free night on a future stay
Double points for tonight
questions.explain_zh: Priya 說 we'd like to comp your next night with us（下次來免費招待一晚）。點數是「照常算」（as if you'd stayed here），不是加倍。

dictation: Your room there has already been paid for, and a taxi's been called.
They'll be added as if you'd stayed here.
It's all been emailed to you.

glossary.zh: （超訂時）被安排到別家飯店的
glossary.definition: (of a hotel guest) sent to another hotel because there is no room for them
a person who books something but does not come and does not cancel
to become balanced over time, so that gains and losses cancel each other
to give something to a customer for free, usually to say sorry (informal)
to make bad news or a bad situation less unpleasant
the freedom to decide what to do in a situation
